correctness.rationale: Set y=|u_prime|^(p-2)u_prime. The equation at gamma=0 gives y(t)=c-A(t), so both Neumann and periodic derivative endpoint conditions require A(T)=0. The two-step primitive traverses [0,M] once in each direction; Neumann fixes c=0 and yields a unique derivative up to an additive solution constant. Periodicity of position requires integral phi_q(c-A)=0, equivalently |c|^q=|c-M|^q, hence c=M/2 uniquely. Integrating absolute derivative on both branches gives Delta_N=(T/q)M^(q-1), Delta_P=(T/q)M^(q-1)/2^q; q=p/(p-1). Independent exact substitutions p=2,3,4 at T=3,M=2 reproduced ratios 1/4,2^(-3/2),2^(-4/3). Any sufficiently large additive shift is positive; no false uniqueness of absolute level claimed.
